Hydrating Fillers

Skin looking dull, dry or tired even with a good routine? Under-eyes hollow, lips thin, or cheeks flatter than they used to be? Hydrating fillers use hyaluronic acid, a moisture magnet your skin already makes, to hydrate from within, soften fine lines and restore lost volume. You'll see results right away, with natural results planned by our doctors.

30–45 minTreatment time
1–3 daysDowntime

Treatment overview

What Are Hydrating Fillers?

Your skin is full of hyaluronic acid (HA), a natural sugar that holds onto water and keeps skin plump, bouncy and smooth. From our mid-20s, the body makes less of it every year. Add sun, pollution and air-conditioning, and skin starts to look dull and dry, with fine lines and hollows appearing.

Hydrating fillers put that HA back. Very soft HA, placed in tiny droplets under the skin, hydrates from within for a smoother, glowing look. Firmer HA, placed in specific spots, restores volume to lips, cheeks, under-eyes, chin and jawline. Most treatments take 30 to 45 minutes, and you see the difference straight away.

Read more: why HA fillers are so safe

HA is already found in your skin, joints and eyes, so the body accepts it well and breaks it down naturally over time. Even better, HA fillers can be dissolved with an enzyme called hyaluronidase if you ever want to change the result or if there's a problem. That's why our doctors use only HA fillers for the face.

Safety still depends on who injects. Our doctors know facial anatomy in detail, use cannulas where they're safer, and always keep hyaluronidase on hand.

1. PlaceHA is placed precisely where your skin needs hydration or support.
2. Attract waterEach molecule draws in water from the surrounding skin.
3. Plump & glowSkin looks smoother, fuller and more radiant within days.

Treatment areas

Where Can Fillers Help? Tap the Face Map

Tap a number on the face, or pick an area from the list, to see what fillers do there, the typical amount and how long it lasts.

Tap a number to see what fillers do there.

Whole-face skin hydration

Tiny droplets of soft hyaluronic acid placed just under the skin across the face. It draws in water from within, so dull, dry or crepey skin looks plumper, smoother and glowing. Ideal if your skin looks tired even with a good skincare routine.

  • Deep, lasting hydration
  • Fine lines soften
  • Better glow and texture
Typical amount1–2 ml
Lasts about6–9 months

Hollow temples

Temples lose volume with age or weight loss, making the face look narrow and tired. A small amount of filler restores a smooth, youthful curve.

  • Softer, fuller upper face
  • Frames the eyes
Typical amount1–2 ml
Lasts about12–18 months

Under-eye hollows (tear troughs)

Hollows under the eyes cast shadows that look like dark circles and make you look tired. A soft filler placed carefully fills the hollow so the area looks brighter and rested.

  • Less shadowing
  • More rested look
  • Very soft, precise product
Typical amount0.5–1 ml (both)
Lasts about9–12 months

Cheek volume

Cheeks flatten with age, which pulls the lower face down. Restoring cheek volume lifts the mid-face and softens the folds below.

  • Lifted mid-face
  • Softer smile lines
  • Natural contour
Typical amount1–2 ml
Lasts about12–18 months

Non-surgical nose shaping

Filler can smooth a bump, lift the tip slightly or straighten the bridge, all without surgery. Results show straight away.

  • Smoother profile
  • No surgery or downtime
Typical amount0.5–1 ml
Lasts about9–12 months

Smile lines (nasolabial folds)

The folds that run from the nose to the corners of the mouth. Filler softens them, often best combined with cheek filler for a natural lift.

  • Softer folds
  • Fresher lower face
Typical amount1–2 ml
Lasts about9–12 months

Lip hydration and shape

From a subtle hydrating lip treatment to more definition and volume. We aim for soft, natural lips that suit your face, never overdone.

  • Hydrated, smoother lips
  • Better shape and balance
  • Softens lip lines
Typical amount0.5–1 ml
Lasts about6–12 months

Marionette lines

Lines from the corners of the mouth down to the chin can make you look sad or tired. Filler supports the area and lifts the mouth corners.

  • Lifted mouth corners
  • Less tired look
Typical amount1 ml
Lasts about9–12 months

Chin and jawline contouring

Filler can project a small chin, balance the profile and sharpen the jawline for a more defined look from every angle.

  • Sharper jawline
  • Balanced profile
  • Works well for men too
Typical amount1–4 ml
Lasts about12–18 months

Not all fillers are the same

Hydrating, Soft or Structural?

Fillers come in different strengths. Your doctor picks the right one for each area, and often uses more than one.

Skin-hydrating HA

Very soft hyaluronic acid placed in tiny droplets just under the skin. It hydrates rather than adds shape.

Best for: dull, dry skin, fine lines, neck, hands
Downtime: 1–2 days of small bumps
Sessions: 1–2, then every 6–9 months

Soft volume fillers

Medium-strength HA for gentle volume where skin is thin and delicate.

Best for: lips, under-eyes, smile lines
Downtime: 2–5 days of swelling
Sessions: top-up every 6–12 months

Structural fillers

Firmer HA that holds shape for lifting and contouring.

Best for: cheeks, chin, jawline, temples, nose
Downtime: 2–5 days of swelling
Sessions: top-up every 12–18 months

What to expect

Benefits of Hydrating Fillers

Hydration, smoothness and volume, with results you can see the same day.

Deep Hydration

Hyaluronic acid holds up to 1,000 times its weight in water, hydrating skin from within.

Softer Fine Lines

Plumps the skin so fine lines and crepey texture smooth out.

Restores Lost Volume

Fills hollows in the cheeks, under-eyes and temples for a fresher, lifted look.

Instant Results

You'll see a difference right away, with the final result settling in 2 to 4 weeks.

Reversible & Safe

HA fillers can be dissolved with an enzyme if ever needed, which makes them one of the safest injectables.

Little Downtime

Mild swelling or a small bruise for a few days. Most people go back to work the same day.

Long-Lasting

Results last from 6 to 18 months, depending on the area and product.

Face, Neck & Hands

Improves skin on the neck, chest and hands too, not just the face.

Swipe to see more

Is it right for you?

Signs Your Skin Needs Hydration

Fillers aren't only about volume. Many people come to us for these everyday skin problems.

Your skin looks flat and lacks glow, even after a good night's sleep and a full skincare routine. Skin-hydrating HA restores moisture deep down, where creams can't reach.

  • Brighter, glowing skin
  • Makeup sits better
  • Results build over 2 to 4 weeks

Skin feels tight and looks crinkly, especially around the eyes, cheeks, neck and hands. HA plumps it from within so it looks smoother and firmer.

  • Smoother texture
  • Bouncier skin
  • Works on neck and hands too

Fine lines that show even when your face is relaxed are often a sign of dehydration. Hydrating HA softens them, and Botox helps with lines caused by movement.

  • Softer fine lines
  • Pairs well with Botox

Hollow under-eyes, flatter cheeks, thinner lips or deeper folds come from losing volume under the skin. Soft and structural fillers restore it naturally.

  • Fresher, rested look
  • Natural lift
  • Instant results

Good to know

Fillers for Indian Skin

Safe for all skin tones
Because HA fillers are injected under the skin, there's no risk of the pigmentation that some lasers and peels can cause on brown skin.
Great for under-eye hollows
Many people with Indian skin have under-eye hollows that look like dark circles. Filler can soften the shadow, while pigment-type dark circles need peels, lasers or creams.
Humidity and sun
Kerala's sun and humidity can leave skin dehydrated under the surface. Daily SPF and hydrating HA keep it plump and protected.
Natural features
We enhance your own features, keeping lips, cheeks and nose in proportion with your face, never copying a trend.

Your appointment

Hydrating Fillers Procedure

A proper consultation and plan come first.

  • Your doctor studies your face, skin and goals, and explains which filler suits each area.
  • Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen, fish oil and vitamin E for a week if your doctor agrees, to reduce bruising.
  • Skip alcohol and smoking for 24 to 48 hours before.
  • Drink plenty of water and avoid very salty food the day before.
  • Plan around big events, as swelling can last a few days.

Treatment takes 30 to 45 minutes, including numbing.

  • Your skin is cleansed and numbing cream is applied.
  • The doctor marks the areas and checks the plan with you.
  • HA is placed with a very fine needle or a blunt cannula.
  • Most fillers contain anaesthetic, so it feels more comfortable as you go.
  • The area is gently shaped, and you see the result in the mirror.

Most people go back to work the same day. The full aftercare plan is below.

  • Mild swelling, redness or a small bruise for a few days.
  • Use a cold pack for 10 minutes at a time.
  • Avoid alcohol, the gym, saunas and strong sun for 24 to 48 hours.
  • Don't press or massage the area unless your doctor tells you to.
  • Come back at 2 weeks for a review.

Results

Hydrating Fillers Results Timeline

You'll see a change straight away, and it gets better as the filler settles.

  1. Same day

    Instant change

    Volume and smoothness show immediately, with some swelling.

  2. Days 3–7

    Swelling settles

    Any swelling or bruising fades and the shape softens.

  3. Weeks 2–4

    Final result

    HA draws in water, skin looks plumper and glowing. We review you at 2 weeks.

  4. 6–18 months

    Top up

    The body slowly breaks down HA. A small top-up keeps results going.

Illustrative model images. Results vary from person to person.

A good fit if you

  • Have dull, dry or dehydrated skin
  • Have hollow under-eyes, thin lips or flat cheeks
  • Want results you can see the same day
  • Want a natural look you can adjust

Not ideal if you

  • Are pregnant or breastfeeding
  • Have an infection, cold sore or active acne in the area
  • Have a big event within a week
  • Mainly have lines from movement (Botox suits these better)

Aftercare

Filler Aftercare

Simple steps that reduce swelling and help your filler settle beautifully.

Do

  • Use a cold pack, 10 minutes at a time
  • Sleep with your head slightly raised
  • Drink plenty of water
  • Keep the area clean

Avoid

  • Touching, pressing or massaging the area
  • Makeup for 12 hours
  • Alcohol, gym, saunas and steam
  • Sleeping face-down

Do

  • Use gentle, hydrating skincare
  • Wear SPF 30 or higher every day
  • Keep drinking plenty of water
  • Come for your 2-week review

Avoid

  • Facials, massages and face rollers
  • Retinoids and strong exfoliants for a few days
  • Smoking and alcohol for a week
  • Dental work for 2 weeks if you can

Contact us straight away if you notice

  • Severe or increasing pain
  • Skin turning white, grey, blue or blotchy near the treated area
  • Changes in your vision
  • Swelling, warmth or redness that gets worse after 2 days

These are rare, but our doctors can treat them quickly, so always call.

Myths vs facts

Filler Myths, Busted

"Fillers always look fake."
Overfilled faces come from too much product in the wrong places. Well-planned filler just looks like a fresher, rested you.
"Fillers are permanent."
HA fillers break down naturally over 6 to 18 months, and can be dissolved sooner if needed.
"Fillers and Botox are the same."
Fillers add hydration and volume. Botox relaxes muscles. They do different jobs and often work together.
"Once you stop, your face sags."
When filler wears off, you simply return to how you would have looked without it. It doesn't stretch or damage your skin.
"Fillers are only for older people."
Many people in their 20s and 30s use hydrating HA for glow, lip hydration and under-eye hollows.

Safety first

Side Effects and Who Should Wait

HA fillers are among the safest injectables. Here's what's normal and when to check with your doctor first.

Common and temporary

  • Mild swelling for 2 to 5 days, more on the lips
  • Redness or tenderness
  • A small bruise
  • Small bumps that settle as the filler softens

Talk to your doctor first if you

  • Are pregnant or breastfeeding
  • Get cold sores (we may give medicine before lip filler)
  • Have an autoimmune condition
  • Take blood thinners
  • Have had a reaction to fillers or lidocaine before

Questions

Hydrating Fillers FAQs

What are hydrating fillers?
Hydrating fillers are injectable gels made of hyaluronic acid (HA), a sugar your skin already makes to hold water. Soft HA hydrates the skin from within, while firmer HA adds volume and shape to areas like the lips, cheeks and under-eyes.
How are hydrating fillers different from regular fillers?
Skin-hydrating HA is very soft and spread in tiny droplets to improve skin quality, glow and fine lines. Regular (volumising) fillers are firmer and placed in specific spots to add shape. Many people benefit from a mix of both.
Are fillers safe?
Yes, when given by trained doctors with genuine, approved products. HA is naturally found in the body, and HA fillers can be dissolved with an enzyme called hyaluronidase if ever needed.
Does it hurt?
Most fillers contain a local anaesthetic, and we apply numbing cream first. Most people feel only mild pressure or pinches.
When will I see results?
Right away. There may be some swelling for a few days, and the final result settles in 2 to 4 weeks as the HA draws in water.
How long do fillers last?
Skin-hydrating HA lasts about 6 to 9 months. Lip filler lasts 6 to 12 months, and cheek, chin and jawline fillers can last 12 to 18 months.
Will I look fake or overdone?
No. Our doctors plan each treatment around your face and use only what you need. You can always start small and add more later, but it's harder to take away.
How many ml of filler will I need?
It depends on the area. Lips usually need 0.5 to 1 ml, under-eyes 0.5 to 1 ml for both sides, and cheeks 1 to 2 ml. Try our syringe estimator above, and your doctor will confirm.
Can fillers be reversed?
Yes. HA fillers can be dissolved with hyaluronidase, usually within a day or two. This is one of the main reasons we use HA fillers.
What's the difference between fillers and Botox?
Fillers add hydration and volume to fill hollows, lips and folds. Botox relaxes muscles to smooth lines caused by movement. They're often used together.
What are the side effects?
Mild swelling, redness, tenderness or a small bruise for a few days is common. Rare risks include lumps or, very rarely, a blocked blood vessel. That's why fillers should only be done by doctors who know facial anatomy and have hyaluronidase on hand.
Who should avoid fillers?
Fillers aren't advised during pregnancy or breastfeeding, with an active skin infection, cold sore or acne in the area, or with certain autoimmune conditions. Tell your doctor about any medicines you take.
Can I have fillers on my neck and hands?
Yes. Skin-hydrating HA works well on crepey neck skin and thin, veiny hands.
Where can I get hydrating fillers in Kerala?
